decision: Worktree Isolation v0 jumps the queue ahead of Plan D (2026-06-08-004, paused pre-lock at its D007) per operator direction 2026-06-10. v0 is a platform primitive: isolation + honesty about who is where — nothing clever.
rationale: Operator: the recent pain (long-lived branches, plan drafts on different bases, cleanup commits, stale stashes, untracked duplicates, merge/close rituals, multiple sessions on one repo state) is exactly the risk profile of Plan D + 008 + Plan B + C+ overlapping. Live demonstration the same day: switching branches to draft THIS plan reverted Plan D's freshly-edited artifacts in the shared tree.

decision: Binding registry lives at $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees.json (install-level, mirroring projects_registry.py: Pydantic v2 extra=forbid, degrade-to-empty+WARN), NOT in tracked plan-dir files. Gate-time snapshots (F002) and override records (F003) DO land in the plan's audit evidence because they are point-in-time facts about a gate run.
rationale: A binding recorded in tracked files would itself conflict across worktrees — the exact failure mode this plan removes. Separation follows the operator-config-separation principle: registry = runtime install state; evidence = audit trail.

decision: owner_actor in v0 is informational only: $DONTPANIC_ACTOR env if set, else user@host. It is recorded and rendered, never enforced. Leases/claims are explicitly out of scope.
rationale: Keep v0 tight; enforcement semantics (lease expiry, steal, multi-agent contention) need real-world signal first — demand-driven scoping.

decision: No force-removal path exists anywhere in v0: deleting a dirty worktree requires the operator to use raw git deliberately. plan close never auto-removes; it may only print the explicit remove command.
rationale: Dirty/untracked state has repeatedly turned out to hold value (or hazards) worth a human look — e.g. Finder-duplicate hazards and deliberately-unmerged work found this week. Fail closed; cleanup is explicit and audited.

decision: Round-1 sufficiency findings (5) resolved by tightening, not overriding: (1) F006 pins base selection — default = repo default branch resolved to a SHA, never the invoking checkout's HEAD implicitly; --base explicit + recorded; unresolvable base refuses. (2) The directive's 'build' path = orchestrate dispatch — added to F002's recording set AND F003's guarded set. (3) plan audit added to F003's guarded set (it writes evidence). (4) DontPanic has NO merge command — merging to main is the operator's external gh ritual (enforce_admins-toggle bypass), so the guarded {lock, audit, close, disposition, dispatch} set IS the complete plan-mutating surface; recorded here so the contract path is named, not implied. (5) F007 now requires a DOM-level render test through the real dashboard page module, not just a payload block.
rationale: All five were plan-level coverage gaps in MY draft against the operator's directive, not new scope. One considered pass per the paid-gate cadence rule.

decision: Round-2 sufficiency findings (2 high / 3 med, branch b_high_severity — round 1 cleared 100%) resolved by pinning: (1) binding schema gains base_sha (resolved commit SHA, pinned at create, never recomputed) distinct from base_ref, and the worktree is created AT base_sha; (2) repo_root derives authoritatively from the plan dir's containing repository, never the invoking checkout (wrong-invoking-repo test); (3) broken-binding includes path-is-not-a-worktree-OF-recorded-repo_root (membership check); (4) F007 wires the REAL dashboard state producer, fixture tests alone insufficient; (5) derivation pinned — path $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees/<repo-dir-name>/<plan-id>, branch plan/<plan-id>, pre-existing branch refuses in v0.
rationale: Second considered pass. All five were pinnable cells, two at high severity (un-dispositionable by design). If round 3 surfaces another fresh layer, STOP and surface the matrix-enumeration pattern to the operator with the rounds ledger instead of a fourth paid call.

decision: STOPPED at round 3 per D006's stop rule and the operator's paid-gate cadence — NO fourth paid lock call without an operator decision. Rounds ledger: r1 = 5 findings (2H/3M, branch d_first_round) -> 100% cleared by D005; r2 = 5 NEW (2H/3M, b_high_severity) -> 100% cleared by D006; r3 = 4 NEW (1H/3M, b_high_severity: snapshot omits base_sha, not-inside-any-worktree refusal unpinned, branch-drift parity HIGH, removal audit lacks removed_by). All four r3 findings were folded into the plan text offline (free) in this commit. The plan is tightened through three layers; every round cleared its predecessor and surfaced the next layer of pin-class cells — the same enumeration shape C0 hit (its D017).
rationale: Severity trumps class, so the r3 high is un-dispositionable under policy v1.0; policy v1.1 (streak-gated high-pin dispositions, plan 2026-06-10-001) is drafted but demand-gated. Operator options, mirroring C0 D017: (a) one more paid re-lock against the now-tightened plan; (b) ledger-justified recorded override (--ignore-sufficiency-findings) citing three 100%-clearance rounds of auditor-classed pins, all already addressed in text; (c) treat this as the second real instance demanded by the v1.1 trigger and lock under the new policy after it ships.

decision: Round-4 (first under policy v1.1, streak=3, 100% clearance again) resolved per the operator fork rule: the HIGH was auditor-classed plan_contract — a REAL fail-open hole in my draft (degrade-to-empty registry + unbound passthrough composes so a corrupt worktrees.json silently disables wrong-worktree protection) — so TIGHTEN, not disposition: corrupt registry now FAILS CLOSED for all guarded entry points (distinct registry-corrupt refusal) while read-only renderers degrade with a visible warning. Also pinned: F005 refuses every unhealthy binding before removal (missing/non-worktree/wrong-repo/detached/drifted, named health check); F007 adds the branch-drifted fixture across all three renderers; F006 pins the default-branch resolution rule (origin/HEAD -> local main-over-master -> refuse).
rationale: Exactly the v1.1 design intent: plan_contract highs stay hard work; the matrix_pin med/low would have been disposition-eligible under the streak but were trivial to pin alongside.
